title: Special Edition: I Reincarnated as the Villainous Princess of *The Shield Hero*—What Do You Think I Should Do?
paragraphs: When I came to, I found myself alone in a luxurious room. Where… on earth… am I? Unable to make sense of the situation, I looked at the vanity nearby.
But what I saw there wasn’t my own familiar face… no. This face was unmistakably that of the villain known as Vitch—the root of all this trouble.
Vaguely, I recall a past life…?　I should have been working as an office lady in modern society.

My name was… what was it again? I can’t quite remember. However, there’s no doubt that the woman reflected in this mirror is the foolish and utterly wicked princess who appears as an enemy in *The Rise of the Shield Hero* and *The Spear Hero’s Redo*.
*The Rise of the Shield Hero*. A work that began as a serialization on the “Let’s Become Novelists” website, was later published in book form, and even adapted into an anime.

It’s the story of Naofumi Iwatani, a college student who came to the library to read, and who, while reading a book titled *The Book of the Four Holy Weapons* that he happened to find, is summoned to another world as the Shield Hero—the hero who saves the world depicted within the book. From this clichéd beginning, he becomes entangled in various conspiracies.

Starting with the other three Heroes—who can’t seem to shake their “video game” mentality—the story follows Naofumi as he fends off conspiracies and false accusations orchestrated by Melromarc, the summoning nation that seeks to persecute him because, from a religious perspective, he is the Shield Hero of an enemy nation. I’ve been reading this series since I was in high school. It’s a work that divides readers—some see it as unconventional yet classic, while others view it as classic yet unconventional—and many find it stressful to read.

After *The Rise of the Shield Hero* concluded, the author wrote a new side story titled *The Spear Hero’s Redo*. This story begins with the Spear Hero—who was portrayed as the main antagonist in *The Rise of the Shield Hero*—getting trapped in a loop in a parallel world. Even though he knows the future, the clumsy Spear Hero—whose personality has changed—tries his best to achieve his ideal future… well, not exactly.

It’s a story about him being infatuated with Filo, one of the heroines from *The Rising of the Shield Hero*, while regretting his past mistakes, struggling to help the Shield Hero, and doing his best to meet Filo. Since the Spear Hero—who’s pretty out there in his own way—tries to force his way through necessary steps, this story reveals events that couldn’t be fully depicted in the main series, *The Rising of the Shield Hero*.

I remember this well because I used to read and enjoy both of these stories a lot. I pored over the characters depicted in the novel’s illustrations and across various media. That’s exactly why there’s no way I could mistake her.

This woman—whose features could almost be called those of a beautiful girl when she puts on a innocent facade, but whose face, when she smiles defiantly, can only be described as that of a villain—is undoubtedly… the villainous princess who would later be known as Vitch. Why is she… that villainous princess?

I gaze at the mirror once more. Hmm, she really is a beauty. When she’s not making that villainous expression and just acting naturally… she doesn’t look entirely out of place as the heroine of a manga aimed at men… How does this even work? At the very least, I don’t think it’s the kind of face that gives her away as a villain at first glance. Well, maybe that’s necessary so the events in the original story make sense.

As I thought that, I looked out the window… and caught a glimpse of someone coming up the stairs. That’s… yeah, no doubt about it. It’s the Four Holy Heroes. I quietly opened the door and called out to the soldier on patrol.
“Excuse me.”
“Ha! What may I do for you, Lady Malty?”
The soldier, startled by my voice, saluted while trying to hide his fear. It seems I still hold some power here. Let’s confirm that, just to be safe.
“Could you tell me what’s happening in the castle right now?”

“Ha! Word has spread throughout the castle that, under the orders of the Three Heroes Church and Aultcray King, the Four Holy Heroes have been successfully summoned! Would you like to attend the audience?”
Just as I thought… it seems I’ve really ended up in another world—the world of *The Rise of the Shield Hero*. In fact, there’s even an option to bring up my status icon right in my field of vision…
“No, but… I plan to observe the situation from the back.”
If I recall correctly… the story went that this princess was actually hiding in the back of the throne room.
“I’m sorry for stopping you. Please return to your duties.”
“Ha!”

The soldier saluted and quickly left the scene. He’s probably talking behind my back right now. Well… to be honest, I’ve read quite a bit of the *Shield Hero* series, and it’s one of my favorite works.
It really fuels my ship-related fantasies, and I’m a big fan of the Faubrey arc featuring the Spear Hero… There’s no doubt I’m that kind of person.
My favorite pairing is Spear × Shield. The other way around is good too. I want to see these two interact.

My mind is racing enough that I’d like to take advantage of this opportunity to pull off all sorts of underhanded schemes… but at the same time, my situation in the *Shield Hero* series is extremely dire. After all, in this series, those who retain memories of their past lives are called “reincarnates,” and I was a pawn of the mastermind behind all the chaos that’s wreaking havoc on the world. So… if I make a wrong move, not only will I be killed, but my very soul might be erased.

Suddenly, I pinch my cheek to see if this is a dream, and a sharp pain shoots through me. Yeah… I really have been reincarnated as Vitch. No… I’ve been possessed by her, actually. This Vitch has all sorts of backstory—or rather, she’s a troublesome presence—and if I’ve been possessed by her, there must be all sorts of complications with her original self… but there’s no strange voice or anything.

…How am I going to survive from here on out? The world is experiencing a phenomenon known as “waves.” If we respond too casually to this crisis, not only will the country continue to fall into ruin, but the world itself might be destroyed. After all, the country is secretly stirring up discord among the Heroes, and it seems this country’s religion believes that after framing and killing the Shield Hero, the world will be saved by the Three Heroes.

Only followers of their own religion will be spared from the time of destruction. A new era will begin with the believers and Heroes who have overcome the crisis. When I look up the religious texts and teachings from the world of my past life, I find quite a few descriptions like that. I can imagine it’s a way to keep believers loyal, but the Three Heroes Church has actually put it into practice.
It may seem foolish, but apocalyptic theories are everywhere. I’m sure they existed in the world of my past life, too.
So, given this situation… what should I do?

Should I, as a “good guy” reincarnate, explain the situation to the heroes and try to get them to believe me? Something like, “I know everything about this story, so please trust me.” But… the moment I say that, if a bomb set by the mastermind behind the scenes were to explode, blowing my head to pieces and even obliterating my soul, that would be the end of the story.

Should I decide to be a bystander, do nothing, and keep my distance from the heroes? That’s not a bad option either. At the very least, if I do nothing, I might be able to avoid putting my own life in danger.

But… if I try anything strange… well. If I use my modern knowledge to do something unnecessary, it seems like ruin is bound to be my fate. There’s no doubt this is the kind of story world where getting too cocky will lead to nothing good.
It’s a bit of a meta way of thinking, though. Neither the Queen nor Princess Melty would complain if I just did nothing.

But… if I remember correctly, wasn’t the plot supposed to go something like this: I’d be made to take responsibility for the Hero’s summoning, and the Queen would end up proposing a marriage alliance with that sadistic King Faubrey…? The Queen is compassionate and wants to avoid marrying me off, but if King Faubrey makes a strong demand, there’s a non-zero chance she won’t be able to refuse and will end up offering me to him. It’s easy to imagine that the fact I was a companion of the Spear Hero was one of the reasons she was able to refuse the marriage proposal in the first place.

Taking action is dangerous; doing nothing is dangerous… Hmm. I need to strike a balance… while making sure the Queen doesn’t marry me off, and without provoking the Heroes… Escaping as a commoner or fleeing the country is probably out of the question—it’d be the work of the Shadow Organization or some covert unit. If I tried something like that, they’d suspect I’m up to something and might go ahead with the marriage anyway.
…It’s starting to feel like I’m in a pretty tight spot. Why did I have to end up as Vitch of all people? If I had to choose, I’d have preferred to be Melty or Raphtalia.

No, actually, maybe a background character—like Keel… or maybe someone low-key like Imiya would be better in this situation? But come to think of it, I’m pretty sure even those characters had pretty tragic pasts and circumstances. I don’t want to end up in a situation like that.

……It’s almost like I’m wondering, “Who would actually be a good choice?”…… that’s when it hit me. Elena, the Lazy Pig! If she manages to worm her way into the Hero’s good graces and just keeps an eye on his mood, she’ll be able to slip away safely. She doesn’t even have a particularly tragic backstory.

Or maybe Filo…? No, that’s a bit too much. Just think about it. If I, a modern-day office worker, were to go around saying, “Filo’s name is Filo!”—that would be problematic in so many ways. Besides, I don’t even know if I could reincarnate as a Filolial in the first place.
It would’ve been better if I’d been a mob Filolial raised by the Spear Hero! Long live reincarnation as a monster!
I unconsciously bit my nails, my teeth grinding. I looked every bit the villainess. With that, I quietly made my way to the audience chamber to peek in on the heroes’ audience.

I have a vague grasp of the castle’s layout from my memories as a princess, so I don’t get lost. I wonder how I should go about this? Since all sorts of people from other worlds have come to this one, it should be hard to make money or gain recognition using modern knowledge.
Just as I was thinking that, it suddenly—an idea occurred to me.
……Is this world I’ve been reincarnated into *The Rise of the Shield Hero*?
Or is it *The Spear Hero’s Second Chance*?

If it’s the former, there are still plenty of possibilities waiting to be tapped. If I stay devotedly by the side of Naofumi Iwatani, the Shield Hero, especially regarding the king’s and the kingdom’s behind-the-scenes schemes, there’s a high chance things will work out.

It’ll be hard work, but the rewards will be great. The queen will appreciate me, so I can avoid being forced into marriage. The Shield Hero, whose personality hasn’t changed, seems to have a bit of an ulterior motive, but he comes across as a perfectly ordinary young man. He’s the kind of otaku who’ll understand if you just talk to him. He’ll believe me even if I hide my true feelings.
If I nurture him properly… yeah. There’s a high chance we’ll survive. As for the shadowy schemes behind the scenes, let’s leave that to the Queen to handle.

As for self-defense, as long as he has knowledge of the series, he’ll be fine. Since I’ve studied the backstory of *The Spear Hero* thoroughly, I’m sure we’ll manage somehow. Besides, there’s a suspicion that *The Shield Hero* comes from the world of a cooking manga, so I’m a little curious just how delicious his food is.
But… if it turns out to be *The Spear Hero* instead, that would be the worst-case scenario.

After all, in the *Spear Hero* reboot, the protagonist—the Spear Hero—basically can’t tell the difference between a woman’s voice and a pig’s squeal. What’s more, I’m considered the absolute worst pig of them all and am even called the “Crimson Swine.” To top it off, there’s a high chance he’ll try to kill me at the first opportunity.

You know… it feels like he’d just suddenly kill me out of the blue. Even if I’m not doing anything in particular, I could just be walking through the castle when suddenly, out of nowhere, a spear pierces my chest from behind and I die… that’s right, hahahaha… BAD END… that’s totally a possibility. It’s like there’s a 1% chance of a death roll every time I take an action, with no save function.
What do you call that? Like that guy in armor.
It’s a bit of a meta thought, but it seems plausible. It’s the kind of development where something happens in future chapters I haven’t read yet.
That’s because *True Spear*, the sequel to *The Spear Hero’s Redo*, hasn’t been completed yet. There might still be countless unexplored parts or landmines lying around.
Anyway… let’s first confirm which one it is. Judging by what happened earlier, he’ll definitely introduce himself during the audience. I quietly slip behind the throne room and prick up my ears.
“I am the king of this realm, Aultcray Melromarc the 32nd. Heroes, raise your heads!”

Ah, so this is Father of this body—the man who would later be called the “Trash King.” He was the “Hero of the Staff” and known as the “Wise King of Wisdom,” and apparently played a significant role in Melromarc’s past.

Nowadays, though… to put it mildly, he’s a “Madao.” He’s just a hopeless old man—or “Madao,” for short. He’s a troublesome old geezer who won’t come to his senses until he loses a few things. I think he’ll listen to me, his daughter, but when it comes to Naofumi Iwatani, the Shield Hero, there’s a high chance he’ll go off the rails. I hope he’ll stop just because I told him to… but since he didn’t seem to back down even after Melty tried to persuade him, it might be difficult.
As I was thinking about this, the king and his entourage began explaining the crisis facing this world.
“I get the gist. So, you’re asking us—who were summoned here—to work for free?”
“That’s a pretty convenient story, isn’t it?”

“We don’t owe you anything, do we? It’d be unbearable to work for free only to be told ‘goodbye’ once peace is restored. Actually, I want to know if there’s even a way for us to get back home—what’s the deal with that?”
“Guh…”
That’s when the Heroes secretly clenched their fists.
“We’ve also prepared financial aid. We truly want you, the Heroes, to protect the world, and we intend to provide a place for you to do so.”
“Don’t think you can keep us on a leash. We’ll cooperate as long as you don’t become our enemies.”
“…I suppose so.”
“Exactly.”
…… Yeah. This flow is definitely *The Shield Hero*. Good, good.

No… I’m starting to feel a little uneasy. If you ask me if I remember the details, I’m a bit iffy on this part of the exchange. But in terms of the flow… it’s definitely right, I think. I listen to the heroes’ self-introductions with my hands clasped together, as if in prayer.
“My name is Ren Amaki. I’m 16 years old and a high school student.”

Yeah, he’s got that shota vibe and is pretty cute. I think he’ll end up having the best personality. He’s the classic hero, isn’t he? Though the events after peace is restored do evoke a lot of sympathy.
But more importantly, what’s coming next!
Shield, shield, shield!
“My name is Motoyasu Kitamura! I’m The Love Hunter!”

It was a spear-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------! I leaned against the wall, unable to help but feel despair at the death flags that were bound to appear from here on out.
What’s going to happen to my life—!? April Fools’ Day
